questions.q: What does 'Batik' mean in textile design?
options: A weaving method that uses brightly colored plastic threads.
A fabric dyeing technique that uses melted wax as a resist material to create patterns.
The process of painting directly onto a canvas with oil colors.
A printing method using carved wooden blocks.
questions.explain: Batik is an ancient resist-dyeing art where hot, melted wax is applied to a cloth to block color from reaching certain areas when the cloth is submerged in dye.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What is the primary difference in the resist methods used by Batik and Tie & Dye?
options: Batik resists dye by using hot wax, whereas Tie & Dye resists dye by folding and tying the fabric tightly.
Batik uses paper tape, whereas Tie & Dye uses glue.
Batik does not use any resist method, whereas Tie & Dye does.
Batik uses plastic wrap, whereas Tie & Dye uses metal rings.
questions.explain: While both are resist-dyeing methods, Tie and Dye achieves the resist physically (via ropes/folds), whereas Batik achieves it chemically/materially (via impermeable wax).

questions.q: Which traditional tool is specifically designed to scoop up melted wax and draw fine lines or dots onto fabric during Batik production?
options: A chisel
A tjanting (canting) tool
A crochet hook
A squeegee
questions.explain: A tjanting (or canting) is a pen-like tool with a small copper reservoir that holds hot wax, allowing the artist to draw detailed patterns onto the cloth.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In the Batik process, how are large areas of the fabric typically covered with wax quickly?
options: By using a tjanting tool.
By using a pair of scissors.
By using paint brushes or foam.
By spraying wax from a machine.
questions.explain: While a tjanting is used for fine details, bristle brushes or foam sponges are used to quickly apply hot wax to larger sections of the fabric.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: After a Batik fabric has been dyed and is fully dried, what is the final step to remove the wax (dewaxing) from the material?
options: Scraping it aggressively with a sharp knife.
Submerging and boiling the fabric in hot water.
Leaving it out in freezing temperatures.
Spraying it with caustic soda.
questions.explain: Boiling the dyed fabric in hot water melts the wax out of the cloth. The wax floats to the top, leaving the fabric clean with the white resisted patterns revealed.
